content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- After a sharp price spike, model overreacts and overshoots in the immediate following days, then gradually corrects.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends in the latter half of the forecast horizon, especially when prices are trending downward.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when historical mean is rising, and lower values when mean is falling — adjust for recent trend direction.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility clustering; underestimates volatility spikes in the final 5–7 days of the forecast.
